Get transcripts, search videos, browse channels, and extract playlists via REST API or YouTube MCP — at scale. Get Started Free View Pricing Works everywhere Powering 15M+ transcripts every month Your browser does not support the video tag. Trusted in production 500K+ Transcripts Processed Daily 49ms median response time. 15M+ transcripts served last month. youtubetotranscript.com Verified Production User ~11M transcripts per month Active recapio.com Verified Production User ~2.8M transcripts per month Active Everything you need from YouTube One API. Full YouTube Access. Transcripts, search, channels, playlists — all in one place. Every feature works via API, MCP, and agent skills. Get Transcripts 1 credit Extract transcripts from any YouTube video — with or without timestamps. Drop the output straight into summarizers, search indexes, or AI pipelines. Summarize videos Study notes Search indexes Content repurposing Request Copy curl " https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/transcript?video_url=dQw4w9WgXcQ&format=json " \ -H " Authorization: Bearer API_KEY " Response { " language ": " en ", " length_seconds ": 1164 , " lengthText ": " 19:24 ", " metadata ": { " title ": " Do schools kill creativity? " }, " transcript ": [ { " text ": " Good morning. How are you? ", " start ": 0.0 , " duration ": 3.2 }, { " text ": " It's been great, hasn't it? ", " start ": 3.2 , " duration ": 2.9 } ] } AI Agent Copy Pull the transcript from this TED talk and give me a bullet-point summary with key quotes get_transcript(video_url="dQw4w9WgXcQ") Here's the summary of "Do schools kill creativity?" by Sir Ken Robinson: • Schools prioritize conformity over creative thinking • Children are educated out of creativity as they age • Key quote: "If you're not prepared to be wrong, you'll never come up with anything original" Want me to extract all the timestamps where he references specific examples? API Reference · MCP Tool Search YouTube 1 credit Search YouTube for videos, channels, or playlists. Filter by type and limit results — perfect for discovery, research, and building content pipelines. Content research Competitor analysis Topic discovery Trend monitoring Request Copy curl " https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/search?q=climate+change&type=video&limit=5 " \ -H " Authorization: Bearer API_KEY " Response { " results ": [ { " type ": " video ", " videoId ": " G9t__9Tmli0 ", " title ": " Climate Change 101 ", " channelTitle ": " National Geographic ", " lengthText ": " 4:00 ", " viewCountText ": " 12M views ", " publishedTimeText ": " 6 years ago ", " hasCaptions ": true }, { " type ": " video ", " videoId ": " SDr2gaSrOCk ", " title ": " Before the Flood ", " channelTitle ": " National Geographic ", " lengthText ": " 1:30:08 ", " viewCountText ": " 8.5M views ", " publishedTimeText ": " 7 years ago ", " hasCaptions ": true } ], " result_count ": 5 , " has_more ": true } AI Agent Copy Find the most-watched climate change explainers on YouTube and compare their key arguments search_youtube(q="climate change", limit=5) Found 5 top climate change videos: 1. "Climate Change 101" (12M views) — broad overview by National Geographic 2. "Before the Flood" (8.5M views) — Leonardo DiCaprio documentary 3. "Causes and Effects of Climate Change" (5.1M views) — National Geographic explainer 4. "Climate Change" (3.8M views) — Kurzgesagt animated breakdown 5. "Is It Too Late To Stop Climate Change?" (2.9M views) — science-focused deep dive Should I pull the transcripts and compare how each one frames the core science? API Reference · MCP Tool Search Inside a Channel 1 credit Search within a specific channel to find videos on any topic. Great for researching a creator's content or finding niche topics in large channels. Research a creator Find specific topics Competitive intelligence Request Copy curl " https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/channel/search?channel=@TED&q=AI&limit=10 " \ -H " Authorization: Bearer API_KEY " Response { " results ": [ { " type ": " video ", " videoId ": " UyyjU8fzEYU ", " title ": " The wonderful implications of computers that can learn ", " channelTitle ": " TED ", " lengthText ": " 16:22 ", " viewCountText ": " 2.3M views ", " publishedTimeText ": " 10 years ago ", " hasCaptions ": true }, { " type ": " video ", " videoId ": " hJP5GqnTrNo ", " title ": " Can AI fix education? ", " channelTitle ": " TED ", " lengthText ": " 10:39 ", " viewCountText ": " 180K views ", " publishedTimeText ": " 1 year ago ", " hasCaptions ": true } ], " result_count ": 6 , " has_more ": true } AI Agent Copy What has TED published about AI in education? I need the top talks to prep for a presentation search_channel(channel="@TED", q="AI education") Found 6 TED talks on AI in education: 1. "Can AI fix education?" — most recent (Aug 2024) 2. "The wonderful implications of computers that can learn" — 2.3M views, great for framing 3. "How AI could save education" — practical classroom applications 4. "What AI means for the future of learning" — policy perspective 5. "Teaching in the age of AI" — teacher's firsthand experience 6. "The AI revolution in education" — broad overview with demos I can fetch the transcripts and pull out the strongest talking points. Want me to do that? API Reference · MCP Tool Browse Channel Videos 1 credit List all videos from any YouTube channel. Ideal for building databases, bulk transcript extraction, or auditing a channel's full content library. Content auditing Video databases Bulk transcripts Channel analysis Request Copy curl " https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/channel/videos?channel=@TED " \ -H " Authorization: Bearer API_KEY " Response { " results ": [ { " videoId ": " iG9CE55wbtY ", " title ": " Do schools kill creativity? ", " channelTitle ": " TED ", " lengthText ": " 19:24 ", " viewCountText ": " 82M views ", " index ": 1 }, { " videoId ": " arj7oStGLkU ", " title ": " Inside the mind of a master procrastinator ", " channelTitle ": " TED ", " lengthText ": " 14:04 ", " viewCountText ": " 65M views ", " index ": 2 } ], " playlist_info ": { " title ": " Uploads from TED ", " numVideos ": " 5,736 videos " }, " has_more ": true } AI Agent Copy Audit TED's full video catalog — how many videos do they have and what are the all-time top performers? get_channel_videos(channel="@TED") TED has 5,200 videos total. Here are the top 3 by views: 1. "Do schools kill creativity?" — 82M views 2. "Inside the mind of a master procrastinator" — 65M views 3. "Your body language may shape who you are" — 61M views Want me to break this down by topic or year, or fetch transcripts for the top 10? API Reference · MCP Tool Track New Uploads Free Check for the latest uploads from any channel — no credits required. Perfect for monitoring, daily recaps, or triggering downstream pipelines. Daily channel recap New content alerts Pipeline triggers Competitor tracking Request Copy curl " https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/channel/latest?channel=@TED " \ -H " Authorization: Bearer API_KEY " Response { " channel ": " @TED ", " results ": [ { " videoId ": " xL2EKQ3Rkos ", " title ": " A bold plan for sustainable energy ", " author ": " TED ", " published ": " 2026-07-24T06:00:00+00:00 ", " viewCount ": " 48K ", " link ": " https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xL2EKQ3Rkos " }, { " videoId ": " k9Rm_SZjKs4 ", " title ": " How AI is transforming medicine ", " author ": " TED ", " published ": " 2026-07-23T14:30:00+00:00 ", " viewCount ": " 112K ", " link ": " https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k9Rm_SZjKs4 " } ], " result_count ": 15 } AI Agent Copy Check if TED posted anything new this week — if it's about AI, summarize it for me get_latest_videos(channel="@TED") TED posted 2 new videos this week. One matches your interest: • "How AI is transforming medicine" (yesterday) — directly relevant • "A bold plan for sustainable energy" (2h ago) — energy/climate topic Fetching the transcript for the AI one now. I'll have a summary for you in a moment. API Reference · MCP Tool Extract Playlist Videos 1 credit Get every video from a YouTube playlist. Process entire courses, lecture series, or curated collections in a single call. Online courses Lecture series Curated collections Batch processing Request Copy curl " https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2/youtube/playlist/videos?playlist=PLrAXtmErZgOe... " \ -H " Authorization: Bearer API_KEY " Response { " results ": [ { " videoId ": " UF8uR6Z6KLc ", " title ": " Lecture 1: Introduction ", " channelTitle ": " Stanford Online ", " lengthText ": " 52:10 ", " viewCountText ": " 1.2M views ", " index ": 1 }, { " videoId ": " 2pWv7GOvuf0 ", " title ": " Lecture 2: Neural Networks ", " channelTitle ": " Stanford Online ", " lengthText ": " 48:35 ", " viewCountText ": " 890K views ", " index ": 2 } ], " playlist_info ": { " title ": " Stanford CS229: Machine Learning ", " numVideos ": " 24 videos " }, " has_more ": true } AI Agent Copy I'm taking this Stanford ML course — get all the lectures and create study notes for each one get_playlist_videos(playlist="PLrAXtmErZgOe...") Found 24 lectures in this playlist (total ~19 hours). I'll process them in order. Starting with Lecture 1: Introduction (52 min) — covers supervised learning, linear regression, and gradient descent. Is TranscriptAPI free? You can start for free: new accounts get 100 free credits, no card required, and one transcript costs one credit. After that, the paid plan is $5 a month for 1,000 credits per month, or $54 a year billed annually. Is TranscriptAPI the same as youtubetranscriptapi? No. TranscriptAPI is a hosted REST API, separate from the open-source YouTubeTranscriptApi Python package, which fetches transcripts from your own machine. TranscriptAPI is managed and also adds YouTube search, channel browsing and playlist extraction. Can I use it from Python or JavaScript? Yes. TranscriptAPI is a REST API, so any language that can send an HTTPS request with a Bearer API key can call it, including Python and JavaScript with Node.js. The API reference includes complete code examples in cURL, Python and JavaScript. Quickstarts: Python , JavaScript , cURL Does it use my YouTube Data API quota? No. You sign in with your own TranscriptAPI credentials: an API key, or OAuth for some MCP clients. You do not need a Google or YouTube Data API key, so no YouTube Data API quota of yours is used. Usage is counted in TranscriptAPI credits instead. Does it work with AI agents (MCP)? Yes. TranscriptAPI runs an MCP server at https://transcriptapi.com/mcp. The MCP docs have setup guides for Claude and ChatGPT, which connect with OAuth, and OpenAI Agent Builder, which uses an API key. It works with any MCP-compatible client, and MCP calls use the same credits as the REST API. TranscriptAPI.com © 2026 Terms Privacy Refund Workflows What to build Docs Contact

Claude Tutorial Complete guide to integrate TranscriptAPI with Claude AI assistant via MCP. Recommended ChatGPT Tutorial Step-by-step guide to connect TranscriptAPI with ChatGPT using OAuth authentication. Agent Builder Tutorial Learn how to set up TranscriptAPI with OpenAI Agent Builder for AI workflows. YouTube Transcript MCP Server Section titled âYouTube Transcript MCP Serverâ TranscriptAPI runs a hosted (remote) MCP server at https://transcriptapi.com/mcp . Add that URL to an MCP client and your AI assistant can fetch YouTube transcripts, search YouTube, and list a channelâs or playlistâs videos. There is nothing to install or host. The server uses the same account, API keys, and credits as the REST API . Server URL: https://transcriptapi.com/mcp Authentication: OAuth 2.1 (Claude, ChatGPT) or an API key sent as a Bearer token (OpenAI Agent Builder and other clients). See Authentication . Tools: 12, covering transcripts, video info and metadata, search, channels, and playlists. See Available Tools . Cost: 2 tools cost no credits. The others use 1 credit per call, or 1 credit per page of results. New accounts get 100 free credits. See Credit Cost . Supported Clients Section titled âSupported Clientsâ Client How it connects Auth Setup guide Claude (claude.ai, Claude Desktop) Custom connector (remote MCP) OAuth Claude guide ChatGPT Plugin on ChatGPT web (custom MCP server) OAuth (Client ID and Secret) ChatGPT guide OpenAI Agent Builder MCP server in an agent workflow API key Agent Builder guide Claude Code TranscriptAPIâs YouTube agent skills (no MCP config needed) API key, set up on first use Claude Code guide Cursor, Windsurf Remote MCP server ( url + headers config) or TranscriptAPIâs YouTube agent skills API key API key configuration OpenClaw TranscriptAPIâs YouTube skill API key, set up on first use OpenClaw guide Any other MCP client Remote MCP server URL OAuth 2.1 or API key Server configuration Writing your own code instead? The REST API exposes the same data. See the Python , JavaScript , and cURL quick starts. What is MCP? Section titled âWhat is MCP?â Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standardized framework that enables AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT to connect directly with external tools and data sources. With TranscriptAPIâs MCP integration, your AI can fetch YouTube transcripts on-demand without manual copy-pasting or switching between applications. Key Benefits: Direct integration into your AI workflow No manual transcript fetching needed Consistent, structured data format Works with any MCP-compatible platform Why Use TranscriptAPI with MCP? Section titled âWhy Use TranscriptAPI with MCP?â TranscriptAPI offers unique advantages for YouTube Transcript MCP integration: Universal Compatibility Section titled âUniversal Compatibilityâ TranscriptAPI works with any platform that supports MCP . Whether your platform uses OAuth for seamless authentication (like Claude and ChatGPT) or requires manual API key configuration (like OpenAI Agent Builder), we provide both options to ensure maximum compatibility. Proven Reliability Section titled âProven Reliabilityâ Battle-tested with major AI platforms Consistent performance across all authentication methods Same powerful transcript extraction engine as our REST API Flexible authentication options (OAuth or API Key) based on your platformâs requirements Prerequisites Section titled âPrerequisitesâ Before setting up TranscriptAPI with MCP, ensure you have: A TranscriptAPI account ( sign up free ) An AI assistant or platform that supports MCP For OAuth: A web browser for the initial authorization For API Key: An active API key from your dashboard MCP Server Configuration Section titled âMCP Server Configurationâ Get your MCP configuration details from the MCP dashboard or use these settings: Property Value Server Name Transcript API Server URL https://transcriptapi.com/mcp Description Use TranscriptAPI to fetch YouTube video transcript automatically Icon Download Icon Quick Setup Visit your MCP dashboard for a personalized setup guide with these configuration details and authentication options tailored to your chosen platform. Authentication Section titled âAuthenticationâ TranscriptAPI supports two authentication methods to work with different MCP platforms: OAuth (Recommended) API Key OAuth Authentication Section titled âOAuth Authenticationâ OAuth provides automatic, secure authentication without manual key management. Supported by: Claude (Dynamic Client Registration - optional credentials) ChatGPT (Static Client Registration - requires Client ID/Secret) Any MCP client supporting OAuth 2.1 Two Registration Methods: TranscriptAPI supports both Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) and Static Client Registration to work with different platforms: 1. Dynamic Client Registration (Claude, optional) Claude and other clients that support DCR can automatically register No Client ID/Secret needed - just add the MCP server URL The client automatically discovers OAuth endpoints and registers itself Youâll be redirected to authorize access (one-time) 2. Static Client Registration (ChatGPT, required) ChatGPT requires Client ID and Client Secret upfront Get your credentials from the MCP Integration dashboard Expand Advanced: Static OAuth Credentials , click Create New Client , name it, then click Generate Credentials Copy your Client ID and Client Secret In ChatGPT on the web, open Plugins , click the plus button, choose Add custom MCP server , enter the server URL, choose OAuth and paste them in Check I understand and want to continue , click Create as a plugin , install the plugin, then type @ in a new chat to select it How it works: Add the MCP server URL to your client For ChatGPT: Add Client ID and Client Secret For Claude: Credentials are optional (DCR supported) The client automatically discovers our OAuth endpoints Youâll be redirected to authorize access (one-time) Tokens are managed automatically with refresh support Technical Details: Uses OAuth 2.1 with both Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591) and Static Registration Authorization server metadata: /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server Protected resource metadata: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource Required scope: mcp:access Access tokens prefixed with oat_ Benefits: No manual key management (for DCR clients) Automatic token refresh Secure, time-limited access Revocable permissions Platform-specific support (ChatGPT and Claude) API Key Authentication Section titled âAPI Key Authenticationâ API Key authentication provides simple, direct access for platforms that donât support OAuth. Required for: OpenAI Agent Builder Custom MCP implementations Development/testing environments How it works: Get your API key from the API Keys dashboard Add it to your MCP client configuration The key is sent as a Bearer token with each request Configuration: the standard url + headers format for remote MCP servers, used by clients such as Cursor and Windsurf: { "mcpServers" : { "transcriptapi" : { "url" : " https://transcriptapi.com/mcp " , "headers" : { "Authorization" : " Bearer sk_your_api_key_here " } } } } Technical Details: Bearer token authentication: Authorization: Bearer sk_... API keys prefixed with sk_ Keys never expire (unless manually revoked) Same key works for both REST API and MCP Security Best Practices: Store keys in environment variables Never commit keys to version control Use separate keys for different environments Rotate keys regularly Available Tools Section titled âAvailable Toolsâ TranscriptAPI exposes 12 tools through MCP: Tool Description Cost get_youtube_transcript Fetch video transcript as markdown or JSON 1 credit get_youtube_video_info Basic metadata + available transcript languages (pick a language first) Free get_video_metadata Rich video metadata; optional details (duration, tags, captions) + related 1 credit search_youtube Search videos, channels, playlists, or movies â with sort/date/duration filters 1 credit/page get_channel_info Channel profile: title, handle, counts, tags, banners, available tabs 1 credit get_channel_latest_videos Get latest ~15 videos from a channel (RSS) Free search_channel_videos Search within a specific channel 1 credit/page list_channel_videos Paginated channel feed â videos (default), shorts , or streams 1 credit/page list_channel_playlists Paginated list of a channelâs playlists 1 credit/page list_channel_posts Paginated community (Posts tab) content 1 credit/page get_channel_sections Curated channel sections ( featured Home, podcasts , releases ) 1 credit list_playlist_videos Paginated list of playlist videos 1 credit/page All channel tools accept flexible input: @handle , full YouTube URL, or UC... channel ID. Which video tool? Use get_youtube_video_info (free) to discover transcript languages before fetching a transcript. Use get_video_metadata (1 credit) for view/like counts, publish date, description, duration, tags, or related videos. get_youtube_transcript Section titled âget_youtube_transcriptâ Extract transcripts from any YouTube video with full control over the output format. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description video_url string required YouTube video URL or 11-character video ID send_metadata boolean true Include video title, author, and thumbnail format string "text" Output format: "text" (markdown) or "json" (structured) include_timestamp boolean true Include timestamps with each segment language string none Comma-separated priority list, e.g. de,en,asr . Omit for English, or the videoâs first available language. asr = auto-generated captions Accepted URL Formats: Full URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ Short URL: https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ Video ID only: dQw4w9WgXcQ Example Usage: // Get transcript as markdown with metadata (default) get_youtube_transcript ({ video_url: " https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ " }) // Returns: { " content " : " # Metadata 
 ## Title: Rick Astley - Never Gonna Give You Up 
 ## Author: RickAstleyVEVO 
 ## Author URL: https://www.youtube.com/@RickAstley 
 ## Thumbnail: https://i.ytimg.com/vi/dQw4w9WgXcQ/hqdefault.jpg 

 # Transcript 
 [0.0s] Never gonna give you up 
 [4.12s] Never gonna let you down... " } // Get JSON format without metadata get_youtube_transcript ({ video_url: " dQw4w9WgXcQ " , format: " json " , send_metadata: false }) // Returns: { " content " : { " transcript " : [ { " text " : " Never gonna give you up " , " start " : 0.0 , " duration " : 4.12 }, { " text " : " Never gonna let you down " , " start " : 4.12 , " duration " : 3.85 } ] } } // Get plain text without timestamps get_youtube_transcript ({ video_url: " dQw4w9WgXcQ " , format: " text " , include_timestamp: false , send_metadata: false }) // Returns: { " content " : " # Transcript 
 Never gonna give you up Never gonna let you down Never gonna run around and desert you... " } Output Formats: Text Format (Default) JSON Format Returns markdown-formatted text with optional metadata header and timestamped transcript lines. # Metadata ## Title: Video Title Here ## Author: Channel Name ## Author URL: https://www.youtube.com/@ChannelName ## Thumbnail: https://i.ytimg.com/vi/VIDEO_ID/hqdefault.jpg # Transcript [ 0.0s ] First line of transcript [ 3.5s ] Second line of transcript [ 7.2s ] Third line of transcript Returns structured data with transcript segments and optional metadata. { "transcript" : [ { "text" : " First line of transcript " , "start" : 0.0 , "duration" : 3.5 }, { "text" : " Second line of transcript " , "start" : 3.5 , "duration" : 3.7 } ], "metadata" : { "title" : " Video Title Here " , "author_name" : " Channel Name " , "author_url" : " https://www.youtube.com/@ChannelName " , "thumbnail_url" : " https://i.ytimg.com/vi/VIDEO_ID/hqdefault.jpg " } } get_youtube_video_info Section titled âget_youtube_video_infoâ Free (no credit used). Basic metadata (title, author, thumbnail) plus the list of available transcript languages â call this before get_youtube_transcript to pick a language. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description video_url string required YouTube video URL or 11-character video ID Each returned language code (e.g. en , or asr-en for auto-generated English) can be passed to get_youtube_transcript âs language parameter. For counts, publish date, description, duration, tags, or related videos, use get_video_metadata . get_youtube_video_info ({ video_url: " dQw4w9WgXcQ " }) get_video_metadata Section titled âget_video_metadataâ Rich video metadata without needing captions: title, view/like-count text, publish date, structured description + links, uploading-channel summary, and thumbnails. Costs 1 credit. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description video_url string required YouTube video URL or 11-character video ID include string[] none Extras: "details" (duration, category, tags, caption tracks) and/or "related" (related videos) Hidden counts are null , never 0 . When details canât be read, details.available is false with a reason instead of guessed values. // Metadata only get_video_metadata ({ video_url: " dQw4w9WgXcQ " }) // With player details + related videos get_video_metadata ({ video_url: " dQw4w9WgXcQ " , include: [ " details " , " related " ] }) search_youtube Section titled âsearch_youtubeâ Search YouTube for videos, channels, playlists, or movies (paginated, ~20 results per page). Returns structured results with video IDs, titles, view counts, and thumbnails, plus a continuation_token for the next page. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description query string none The search query (first call). search_type string "video" Type of search: "video" , "channel" , "playlist" , or "movie" (first call only). sort string "relevance" First-page sort: "relevance" or "views" . upload_date string none First-page upload window (videos only): hour , today , week , month , year . duration string none First-page duration bucket (videos only): short (under 4m), medium (4â20m), long (over 20m). continuation string none Pagination token from previous response (subsequent calls). Provide either query (first call) or continuation (next pages) â not both. Filters apply to the first call only ; the continuation token already encodes them. An empty page can come back while has_more is true â keep following the token until has_more is false . Costs 1 credit per page. Example Usage: // First call search_youtube ({ query: " TED talk artificial intelligence " , search_type: " video " }) // Returns: { " content " : { " results " : [ { " video_id " : " abc123 " , " title " : " The future of AI | TED Talk " , " channel " : " TED " , " view_count " : " 2.5M views " , " published " : " 2024-03-15 " , " thumbnail " : " https://i.ytimg.com/vi/abc123/hqdefault.jpg " } // ... more results ], " continuation_token " : " 4qmFsgKlARIY... " , " has_more " : true } } // Next page â use continuation token search_youtube ({ continuation: " 4qmFsgKlARIY... " }) get_channel_latest_videos Section titled âget_channel_latest_videosâ Get the ~15 most recent videos from a YouTube channel via RSS. Free â no credits consumed. When YouTubeâs feed is unavailable, published is approximate: the list then comes from the channelâs uploads, and publish times are worked out from times like â9 hours agoâ. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description channel string required Channel identifier: @handle , channel URL, or UC... ID Accepted Input Formats: Handle: @TED URL: https://www.youtube.com/@TED Channel ID: UCsT0YIqwnpJCM-mx7-gSA4Q Example Usage: get_channel_latest_videos ({ channel: " @TED " }) // Returns: { " content " : { " channel " : { " name " : " TED " , " url " : " https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCsT0YIqwnpJCM-mx7-gSA4Q " }, " results " : [ { " video_id " : " xyz789 " , " title " : " The next breakthrough in AI " , " published " : " 2024-06-01 " , " thumbnail " : " https://i.ytimg.com/vi/xyz789/hqdefault.jpg " } // ... up to ~15 results ] } } search_channel_videos Section titled âsearch_channel_videosâ Search for videos within a specific YouTube channel (paginated, ~30 results per page). Costs 1 credit per page. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description channel string none Channel identifier: @handle , channel URL, or UC... ID (first call). query string none Search query within the channel (first call). continuation string none Pagination token from previous response (subsequent calls). Provide either ( channel + query ) (first call) or continuation (next pages) â not both. Example Usage: // First call search_channel_videos ({ channel: " @TED " , query: " education " }) // Returns: { " content " : { " results " : [ { " video_id " : " def456 " , " title " : " The future of education | TED Talk " , " view_count " : " 1.2M views " , " published " : " 2024-01-20 " , " thumbnail " : " https://i.ytimg.com/vi/def456/hqdefault.jpg " } // ... more results ], " continuation_token " : " 4qmFsgKlARIY... " , " has_more " : true } } // Next page â use continuation token search_channel_videos ({ continuation: " 4qmFsgKlARIY... " }) list_channel_videos Section titled âlist_channel_videosâ List a channelâs feed with pagination. Use tab to choose the uploads feed (default, ~100/page), Shorts, or live streams (~48/page). Costs 1 credit per page. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description channel string none Channel identifier: @handle , URL, or UC... ID (first call) tab string "videos" Which feed: videos (uploads), shorts , or streams (live). Repeat the same tab when paginating. continuation string none Pagination token from previous response (subsequent calls) Provide either channel (first call) or continuation (next pages) â not both. Example Usage: // First call â start listing list_channel_videos ({ channel: " @TED " }) // Returns: { " content " : { " results " : [ { " video_id " : " ghi789 " , " title " : " How AI could empower any business " , " view_count " : " 800K views " , " published " : " 2024-05-10 " } // ... ~100 results ], " continuation_token " : " Ehl... " , " has_more " : true } } // Next page â use continuation token list_channel_videos ({ continuation: " Ehl... " }) get_channel_info Section titled âget_channel_infoâ A channelâs profile: title, @handle , verified flag, subscriber/video-count text, description, keywords, tags, thumbnails, banners, and the tabs it exposes. Not paginated. Costs 1 credit. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description channel string required Channel identifier: @handle , URL, or UC... ID Counts are display strings (e.g. 27.8M subscribers ) and null when YouTube hides them â never 0 . Check availableTabs before calling get_channel_sections or list_channel_videos with a tab . get_channel_info ({ channel: " @TED " }) list_channel_playlists Section titled âlist_channel_playlistsâ Paginated list of the playlists on a channel (id, title, URL, video-count text, thumbnails). Costs 1 credit per page. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description channel string none Channel identifier: @handle , URL, or UC... ID (first call) continuation string none Pagination token from previous response (subsequent calls) Provide either channel or continuation â not both. Pass a returned playlist id to list_playlist_videos to get its videos. list_channel_playlists ({ channel: " @TED " }) list_channel_posts Section titled âlist_channel_postsâ Paginated list of a channelâs community (Posts tab) content â text, publish time, like-count text, and attachments (image, multi-image, video, playlist, or poll). Costs 1 credit per page. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description channel string none Channel identifier: @handle , URL, or UC... ID (first call) continuation string none Pagination token from previous response (subsequent calls) Provide either channel or continuation â not both. Channels without a community tab return an empty results list (not an error). list_channel_posts ({ channel: " @TED " }) get_channel_sections Section titled âget_channel_sectionsâ The curated, grouped sections of a channel page â titled shelves of videos, playlists, shorts, or featured channels, in the channelâs own order. Not paginated. Costs 1 credit. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description channel string required Channel identifier: @handle , URL, or UC... ID tab string "featured" Which curated page: featured (Home), podcasts , or releases podcasts and releases exist only on channels that have them (empty results otherwise â call get_channel_info to see a channelâs tabs). get_channel_sections ({ channel: " @TED " }) get_channel_sections ({ channel: " @TED " , tab: " releases " }) list_playlist_videos Section titled âlist_playlist_videosâ List videos in a YouTube playlist with pagination (~100 per page). Costs 1 credit per page. Parameters: Parameter Type Default Description playlist string none Playlist URL or ID starting with PL , UU , LL , FL , or OL (first call) continuation string none Pagination token from previous response (subsequent calls) Provide either playlist (first call) or continuation (next pages) â not both. Example Usage: // First call â start listing list_playlist_videos ({ playlist: " UUAuUUnT6oDeKwE6v1NGQxug " }) // Returns: { " content " : { " results " : [ { " video_id " : " jkl012 " , " title " : " Introduction to Machine Learning " , " channel " : " TED-Ed " , " published " : " 2024-02-15 " } // ... more results ], " continuation_token " : " Qmx... " , " has_more " : true } } // Next page â use continuation token list_playlist_videos ({ continuation: " Qmx... " }) Platform Integration Section titled âPlatform Integrationâ TranscriptAPI MCP works with any platform that supports the Model Context Protocol . Here are guides for popular platforms: Tested Platforms Section titled âTested Platformsâ Connect to Claude - OAuth authentication support Connect to ChatGPT - OAuth authentication support Connect to OpenAI Agent Builder - API key authentication Universal Compatibility Section titled âUniversal Compatibilityâ TranscriptAPI works with any tool, framework, or custom implementation that supports MCP: OAuth-enabled platforms : Automatic authentication and token management API key platforms : Manual configuration with your TranscriptAPI key Custom implementations : Choose the authentication method that fits your needs Future-Proof Integration As new MCP-compatible platforms emerge, TranscriptAPI will work with them out of the box. Our standards-compliant implementation ensures long-term compatibility. Credit Usage & Rate Limits Section titled âCredit Usage & Rate Limitsâ MCP requests consume credits and are subject to rate limits just like REST API calls: Credit Cost Section titled âCredit Costâ Tool Cost get_youtube_transcript 1 credit get_youtube_video_info Free get_video_metadata 1 credit search_youtube 1 credit per page get_channel_info 1 credit get_channel_latest_videos Free search_channel_videos 1 credit per page list_channel_videos 1 credit per page list_channel_playlists 1 credit per page list_channel_posts 1 credit per page get_channel_sections 1 credit list_playlist_videos 1 credit per page Only charged on successful (HTTP 200) responses Failed requests (4xx, 5xx) donât consume credits Rate Limits Section titled âRate Limitsâ 200 requests per minute on Starter Monthly, 300 requests per minute on Starter Annual and OpenClaw (more on request) Limits apply per account , shared by all your API keys and OAuth tokens See API Rate Limits for detailed information and best practices. Monitor Your Usage MCP tools may make multiple requests during a conversation. Monitor your credit usage in the dashboard to avoid unexpected consumption. Error Handling Section titled âError Handlingâ All MCP tools return user-friendly error messages that AI assistants can understand and communicate: Common Errors Section titled âCommon Errorsâ Error Code Description Retry? Solution 401 Invalid authentication â Check your API key or re-authorize OAuth 402 Insufficient credits â Purchase more credits or upgrade plan 404 Transcript not available â Video may not have captions or be private 408 Timeout / Retry â Temporary failure - retry after 1-5 seconds 422 Invalid YouTube URL â Provide a valid YouTube URL or video ID 429 Rate limit exceeded â Wait before retrying (see Retry-After header) 500 Server error â ï¸ Temporary issue, contact support if persistent 503 Service unavailable â Service temporarily down - retry after 1-5 seconds Error Response Format Section titled âError Response Formatâ Errors are returned in a format that AI assistants can easily interpret: { "content" : " Unable to fetch transcript: Payment required. You have no credits remaining. Please purchase more credits at https://transcriptapi.com/dashboard/billing " } The AI assistant will communicate these errors naturally to the user. Best Practices Section titled âBest Practicesâ Security Section titled âSecurityâ OAuth platforms : Let the platform handle token storage and refresh API key platforms : Store keys in environment variables, never in code Rotate API keys regularly for enhanced security Monitor usage through the dashboard to detect anomalies Performance Section titled âPerformanceâ Batch requests when possible to stay within rate limits Cache transcripts locally if you need them multiple times Handle 402 errors gracefullyâinform users about credit status Implement exponential backoff for retries on 408/429/503 errors Integration Tips Section titled âIntegration Tipsâ Test with common videos first to ensure configuration works Provide context to the AI about video content for better responses Use metadata to give AI information about video source and author Choose the right format : JSON for structured processing, text for natural language Development Workflow You can develop and test with API keys for quick setup, then switch to OAuth for production deployments when supported by your platform. Troubleshooting Section titled âTroubleshootingâ OAuth Issues Section titled âOAuth Issuesâ âAuthorization failedâ : Clear browser cookies and try again âInvalid redirectâ : Ensure youâre using the latest MCP client version Token expiration : OAuth tokens auto-refresh; if issues persist, re-authorize API Key Issues Section titled âAPI Key Issuesâ âInvalid API keyâ : Verify key starts with sk_ and is active in dashboard âNo creditsâ : Check credit balance at /dashboard/billing Key not working : Ensure no extra spaces when copying the key General Issues Section titled âGeneral Issuesâ No transcript returned : Video might not have captions available Slow responses : Check if video is very long (>2 hours) Connection errors : Verify your internet connection and firewall settings Next Steps Section titled âNext Stepsâ Ready to get started? Hereâs what to do next: Get your credentials : Sign up and get an API key or prepare for OAuth Choose your platform : Select from our platform-specific guides Configure MCP : Follow the configuration examples above Test it out : Try fetching a transcript from a YouTube video Explore the API : Check our REST API Reference for advanced usage Need live testing? Try our Swagger UI to experiment with the API directly. Frequently Asked Questions Section titled âFrequently Asked Questionsâ What is a YouTube transcript MCP server? It is an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that gives an AI assistant a tool for fetching YouTube transcripts. TranscriptAPIâs server is hosted at https://transcriptapi.com/mcp , so the assistant calls it directly and you donât run anything on your own machine. Besides transcripts, it can search YouTube and list channel and playlist videos. Which AI assistants work with the TranscriptAPI MCP server? Claude and ChatGPT connect with OAuth, and OpenAI Agent Builder connects with an API key. Each has a step-by-step guide: Claude , ChatGPT , OpenAI Agent Builder . Other clients that support remote MCP servers can connect with OAuth 2.1 or an API key sent as a Bearer token. See Supported Clients . Do I need to install or host anything? No. TranscriptAPI hosts the MCP server. You add the server URL in your AI client, then either sign in through OAuth or add your API key. How much does the YouTube MCP server cost? New accounts get 100 free credits with no card required. The get_youtube_video_info and get_channel_latest_videos tools cost no credits. The other tools use 1 credit per call, or 1 credit per page for paginated results. Failed requests donât use credits. Calls still need a verified email and an account with credits or a plan. Paid plans start at $5 per month for 1,000 credits. See Credit Cost . Is the MCP server the same as the REST API? It uses the same account, API keys, and credits as the TranscriptAPI REST API and the same transcript extraction. You can try a workflow in an AI assistant and later call the REST API from your own code. Can the MCP server get transcripts in other languages? Yes. The get_youtube_video_info tool, which costs no credits, lists the transcript languages a video offers, and get_youtube_transcript accepts a language priority list such as de,en . Codes starting with asr are YouTubeâs auto-generated captions. Related Section titled âRelatedâ API Reference Complete REST API documentation with examples and parameters. Getting Started Quick start guide for TranscriptAPI basics and setup. Contact Support Get help with technical issues or account questions. Next Steps Frequently Asked Questions Related Connect YouTube to ChatGPT with the TranscriptAPI connector To connect YouTube to ChatGPT so it can read video transcripts, add TranscriptAPIâs hosted MCP server as a plugin. In ChatGPT on the web, open Plugins , click the plus button, choose Add custom MCP server , enter https://transcriptapi.com/mcp and choose OAuth, using a Client ID and Client Secret from your TranscriptAPI dashboard . Create and install the plugin, then type @ in a new chat to select it. Learn how to connect TranscriptAPIâs YouTube Transcript MCP to ChatGPT and fetch YouTube video transcripts directly in your conversations. This step-by-step guide walks you through getting credentials, adding the connector as a ChatGPT plugin, and using it effectively. Note The video was recorded with ChatGPTâs older Developer Mode flow. Follow the written steps below for the current setup. What is the TranscriptAPI MCP connector? Section titled âWhat is the TranscriptAPI MCP connector?â TranscriptAPIâs MCP connector lets ChatGPT call TranscriptAPIâs hosted YouTube transcript API directly from a conversation, using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) â the same open standard TranscriptAPI also supports for Claude and OpenAI Agent Builder. Once connected, ChatGPT can fetch a videoâs transcript, search YouTube, browse a channelâs videos, or page through a playlist, without you copying captions in by hand. For a general explanation of what a YouTube transcript API does under the hood, see the YouTube Transcript API developer guide . Prerequisites Section titled âPrerequisitesâ Before getting started, ensure you have: ChatGPT on the web, with a plan and permission to create plugins with custom MCP servers: Free: creating plugins isnât included. Go and Plus: OpenAIâs pricing page includes creating plugins, but its MCP help article doesnât mention these plans. Check that you see Add custom MCP server before you start. Pro: custom servers can connect with read permissions. Business: only admins and owners can create the plugin. Enterprise and Edu: an admin may need to give you permission. A TranscriptAPI account ( sign up free ) 10 minutes to complete the setup ChatGPT MCP support BETA ChatGPTâs full MCP support is in beta. You may encounter occasional issues like: Tool calls that appear to fail but actually succeed Connection errors that require refreshing the connector Parallel searches that override MCP responses These are known ChatGPT beta issues. If you experience problems, try the troubleshooting steps in this guide or consider using Claude for a more stable experience. Part 1: Get your OAuth credentials Section titled âPart 1: Get your OAuth credentialsâ Open the MCP Integration page In your TranscriptAPI dashboard, open MCP Integration in a new tab. Create a client Expand Advanced: Static OAuth Credentials and click Create New Client . Name the client and click Generate Credentials . If you already have a client, use its Client ID and Client Secret. Copy the credentials Copy both the Client ID and Client Secret . Youâll need them in Part 2. Save Your Credentials The Client Secret is only shown once when first generated or regenerated. Make sure to copy it immediately and store it securely. If you lose it, you can regenerate a new secret, but the old one will stop working. Part 2: Add TranscriptAPI Connector Section titled âPart 2: Add TranscriptAPI Connectorâ ChatGPT adds custom MCP servers as plugins. You donât need to turn on Developer Mode first. Open Plugins In ChatGPT on the web, open Plugins . Add a custom MCP server Click the plus button, then choose Add custom MCP server . Enter the name and description Enter a name, such as âTranscript APIâ. The description is optional. You can copy both from the MCP Integration page. Enter the server URL This is the most important step. Under Connection , enter the server URL: https://transcriptapi.com/mcp . Add Client ID and Client Secret to ChatGPT Choose OAuth as the authentication method, then paste your Client ID and Client Secret . Security Best Practice Never share your Client Secret publicly. Itâs tied to your TranscriptAPI account and allows access to your API credits. Acknowledge the risk warning Review the warning and check I understand and want to continue . Create the plugin Click Create as a plugin , then review the tools it finds. Install the plugin Find the plugin in your personal plugins, or in the workspace where you created it, and install it. Part 3: Authorize Connection Section titled âPart 3: Authorize Connectionâ OAuth Flow With Client ID and Client Secret configured, ChatGPT will handle the OAuth authorization flow automatically. You may still be redirected to TranscriptAPI to authorize access, but the credentials you provided ensure ChatGPT can complete the authentication process. After creating and installing the plugin, youâll need to authorize it to access your TranscriptAPI account. TranscriptAPI authorization page Youâll be redirected to TranscriptAPIâs authorization page. If youâre not already logged in, youâll need to sign in first. Review permissions Check the box to acknowledge that ChatGPT will be able to use your API credits and access the MCP server. Complete authorization Click âAuthorizeâ to grant ChatGPT access to TranscriptAPI through OAuth. Connection successful Youâll see a success message confirming that TranscriptAPI is now connected to your ChatGPT account. Part 4: Using the YouTube Transcript MCP Section titled âPart 4: Using the YouTube Transcript MCPâ Now youâre ready to fetch YouTube transcripts directly in ChatGPT! Start a new chat Open a new conversation in ChatGPT on the web. Select the plugin Type @ in the prompt box and select the TranscriptAPI plugin by the name you gave it. Request a transcript Paste a prompt like: âFetch transcript and summarize this long video for me https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIDEO_ID â Send your request Click the send button to submit your transcript request. Confirm tool usage if asked ChatGPT may ask you to confirm the tool call, depending on your permissions. Approve it to proceed. Success! Transcript fetched The MCP will successfully fetch the YouTube transcript, and ChatGPT will process it according to your request (summarize, analyze, translate, etc.). Example Prompts Section titled âExample Promptsâ Here are some effective ways to use TranscriptAPI in ChatGPT: Summarize a Video Section titled âSummarize a Videoâ Fetch the transcript and summarize this TED talk for me: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UF8uR6Z6KLc Translate a Transcript Section titled âTranslate a Transcriptâ Get the transcript from this video and translate it to Spanish: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UF8uR6Z6KLc Search YouTube Section titled âSearch YouTubeâ Search YouTube for "quantum computing explained" and tell me what the top results cover. Browse a Channel Section titled âBrowse a Channelâ Show me the latest videos from @natgeo and summarize the 3 most recent ones. Search Within a Channel Section titled âSearch Within a Channelâ Search @TED for videos about education. List what you find. Process a Playlist Section titled âProcess a Playlistâ List the videos in this playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=UUAuUUnT6oDeKwE6v1NGQxug Get the transcript for the first video and create study notes. How this compares to other ways to get YouTube transcripts Section titled âHow this compares to other ways to get YouTube transcriptsâ The MCP connector is one of several ways to get transcript text out of YouTube. Hereâs an honest comparison: Approach What it is Strengths Trade-offs TranscriptAPI MCP connector A hosted YouTube transcript API exposed to ChatGPT as an MCP tool Nothing to install or host; OAuth-based setup (this guide); same infrastructure as TranscriptAPIâs REST API (49ms median response time, 15M+ transcripts/month); also adds search, channel, and playlist tools Requires a TranscriptAPI account and credits after the free tier; requires a ChatGPT plan that can create plugins with MCP servers (full MCP support is in beta) youtube-transcript-api (Python) A free, open-source Python package that reads YouTubeâs own caption tracks No signup or API key; quick to try locally; works without a headless browser Runs on your own servers, so it inherits YouTubeâs cloud-IP blocking; Python-only; no channel, playlist, or search endpoints; no built-in MCP support â connecting it to ChatGPT means writing and hosting your own MCP wrapper DIY yt-dlp scraping A free, open-source command-line tool for downloading YouTube video/audio, which can also save caption files Extremely flexible; large, active community; not limited to transcripts Not an API or an MCP connector â output is subtitle files (VTT/SRT) you parse yourself; same YouTube anti-scraping exposure as any direct-scraping approach; you own the hosting, scheduling, and keeping it updated as YouTube changes Generic web-scraping APIs / actor platforms General-purpose scraping infrastructure (e.g., actor-based platforms) pointed at YouTube pages Flexible for one-off jobs and mixed data beyond transcripts (comments, page metadata) Not transcript-specialized â pricing, latency, and output schema vary by job/actor; typically no dedicated MCP surface for AI assistants; more setup than a purpose-built transcript API If youâre already using the Python youtube-transcript-api package and hitting IP blocks or parser errors, see the migration guide . For a broader look at hosted transcript API options, see Best YouTube Transcript APIs Compared . Troubleshooting Section titled âTroubleshootingâ Common ChatGPT Beta Issues Section titled âCommon ChatGPT Beta Issuesâ Beta Limitations Due to ChatGPTâs beta status, you may encounter these issues: âUnable to fetch transcriptâ (but it actually worked) Section titled ââUnable to fetch transcriptâ (but it actually worked)â Symptom : ChatGPT says it couldnât fetch the transcript, but if you ask again, it has the content. Solution : This happens when ChatGPT runs a parallel search that overrides the MCP response. Simply ask ChatGPT to use the transcript it already fetched. âMCP tool cannot be calledâ errors Section titled ââMCP tool cannot be calledâ errorsâ Symptom : Random errors about the MCP tool being unavailable. Solution : In ChatGPTâs settings, open the details page for the TranscriptAPI plugin Refresh it to pull the tools again, and authorize again if asked Try your request again Connection timeout or slow responses Section titled âConnection timeout or slow responsesâ Symptom : The tool takes a long time or times out. Solution : For very long videos (>2 hours), the transcript fetch may take longer Try again with a shorter video first to test the connection Check your TranscriptAPI credit balance TranscriptAPI-Specific Issues Section titled âTranscriptAPI-Specific Issuesâ No credits remaining Section titled âNo credits remainingâ Symptom : Error message about payment required or no credits. Solution : Purchase more credits in your TranscriptAPI dashboard. Video has no transcript available Section titled âVideo has no transcript availableâ Symptom : 404 error or âtranscript not availableâ message. Solution : The video may: Not have captions enabled Be private or age-restricted Be deleted or unavailable in your region Need More Help? Section titled âNeed More Help?â If you continue experiencing issues: For ChatGPT beta issues : Consider using Claude for a more stable MCP experience For TranscriptAPI issues : Contact support with your specific error message For general MCP questions : See our MCP documentation Next Steps Section titled âNext Stepsâ Now that youâve successfully connected TranscriptAPI to ChatGPT, explore these resources: Learn about MCP authentication options for different platforms Discover all available MCP parameters for advanced usage Check your credit usage and limits Try TranscriptAPI with other AI platforms Frequently Asked Questions Section titled âFrequently Asked Questionsâ Do I need to install anything to use TranscriptAPI in ChatGPT? No. The MCP connector runs on TranscriptAPIâs servers â you add the server URL and OAuth credentials in ChatGPTâs Plugins, then authorize it (see Part 2 and Part 3 above). No local libraries, scrapers, or servers to run. Is a âYouTube captions APIâ the same thing as a transcript API? The terms are often used interchangeably. TranscriptAPIâs MCP connector returns the same underlying caption data (manual or auto-generated) as TranscriptAPIâs REST API. See captions vs. transcripts vs. subtitles for the terminology breakdown. Can I use the same TranscriptAPI account for LLM apps outside ChatGPT? Yes. The MCP connector and the REST API share the same account, credits, and rate limits, so you can also call TranscriptAPI directly from your own LLM app or agent. See giving AI agents access to YouTube data via MCP . Do I need a paid ChatGPT plan? You need a plan that can create plugins with custom MCP servers, and the Free plan canât create plugins. OpenAIâs help article covers Business (admins and owners), Enterprise and Edu (may need admin permission), and Pro (read permissions). Its pricing page also lists creating plugins on Go and Plus, but the help article doesnât mention those plans, so check that you see Add custom MCP server before you start. See Prerequisites above. Does the connector cost anything beyond my ChatGPT subscription? TranscriptAPI is metered separately from ChatGPT: new accounts get 100 free credits, and paid plans start at $5/month. Fetching a transcript costs 1 credit; listing a channelâs latest videos is free. See MCP credit usage and rate limits for the full breakdown. Part 1: Add TranscriptAPI Connector Section titled âPart 1: Add TranscriptAPI Connectorâ Letâs begin by adding TranscriptAPI as a custom connector in Claude. Connect to TranscriptAPI Click âConnectâ to begin the authorization process. Claude Fetches Transcript Automatically Watch as Claude seamlessly calls the TranscriptAPI tool to retrieve the video transcript. Success! Advanced Tips Section titled âAdvanced Tipsâ Free Channel Checks : Browsing a channelâs latest videos costs no credits â use it to scout before spending credits on transcripts. Batch Processing : Paste all URLs at once instead of one by one. Claude fetches multiple transcripts simultaneously. Focused Questions : Instead of âsummarize these videos,â try âidentify the three main disagreements between these perspectives.â Output Formats : Specify tables, bullet points, or narrative summaries. This guide provides step-by-step instructions with screenshots. What is OpenAI Agent Builder? Section titled âWhat is OpenAI Agent Builder?â OpenAI Agent Builder is a visual, no-code platform for creating and deploying AI agents with complex workflows. It features a drag-and-drop interface that lets you connect various tools and services without writing code. The platformâs Model Context Protocol (MCP) support makes it ideal for integrating external services like TranscriptAPI. Better Beta Experience Unlike ChatGPTâs beta MCP implementation which can have stability issues, OpenAI Agent Builderâs beta provides a more reliable experience for MCP tools. The platform handles tool calls consistently and provides clear error messages when issues occur. Prerequisites Section titled âPrerequisitesâ Before starting, ensure you have: An OpenAI account with access to Agent Builder (available with API access) A TranscriptAPI account ( sign up free ) An active TranscriptAPI API key from your dashboard A YouTube video URL to test with Part 1: Create Your Agent Workflow Section titled âPart 1: Create Your Agent Workflowâ Letâs start by creating a new workflow in OpenAI Agent Builder. Access OpenAI Agent Builder Navigate to the OpenAI Agent Builder platform and sign in with your OpenAI credentials. Configure the Agent Node Click on the default Agent node that appears in your workflow canvas. This is where youâll add the TranscriptAPI MCP integration. Part 2: Add TranscriptAPI MCP Server Section titled âPart 2: Add TranscriptAPI MCP Serverâ Now weâll add the TranscriptAPI MCP server to your agent. Open Tools Configuration In the agent configuration panel, locate the âToolsâ section and click the â+â icon to add a new tool. Select MCP Server From the tool options, choose âMCP serverâ to add an MCP integration. Configure Server Details Click on the âServerâ field to begin configuring the MCP connection. Part 3: Configure TranscriptAPI Connection Section titled âPart 3: Configure TranscriptAPI Connectionâ Letâs set up the connection details for TranscriptAPI. Youâll need information from your TranscriptAPI dashboard. Get Configuration Details Open the TranscriptAPI MCP Integration page in a new tab. Youâll copy configuration details from here. Enter Server URL Paste the MCP server URL: https://transcriptapi.com/mcp Copy and Enter MCP Name Copy the MCP name from TranscriptAPI (typically âTranscriptAPIâ). Enter it in the name field. Copy and Enter Description Copy the MCP description from your dashboard. Paste it into the description field. Part 4: Set Up API Key Authentication Section titled âPart 4: Set Up API Key Authenticationâ OpenAI Agent Builder requires API key authentication for MCP servers. OAuth is not currently supported. View Authentication Options Youâll see both OAuth and API Key options. OAuth is recommended for supported platforms, but Agent Builder requires API Key authentication. Select API Key Authentication Click on âAPI Key / Access Tokenâ to use the required authentication method. Copy Your API Key From the TranscriptAPI dashboard, click the copy button to get your API key. Enter API Key Paste your API key into the authentication field in Agent Builder. Connect to TranscriptAPI Click the âConnectâ button to establish the connection. Authentication Success Agent Builder will authenticate with TranscriptAPI and load the available MCP tools. Add the Tool Click âAddâ to include the TranscriptAPI MCP in your agentâs toolset. Part 5: Configure Agent Instructions Section titled âPart 5: Configure Agent Instructionsâ Now configure your agent to use the TranscriptAPI MCP effectively. Add Agent Instructions In the agentâs instruction field, add clear guidance about when to use the YouTube Transcript MCP. For example: âWhen you see a YouTube video link, use the TranscriptAPI MCP tool (get_youtube_transcript) to fetch the video transcript. Then process the transcript according to the userâs request (summarize, analyze, translate, etc.).â Name Your Agent Give your agent a descriptive name like âTranscriptAPI Agentâ or âYouTube Transcript Assistantâ. Part 6: Test Your Integration Section titled âPart 6: Test Your Integrationâ Letâs test the YouTube Transcript MCP integration to ensure everything works correctly. Enter Preview Mode Click the âPreviewâ button to test your agent workflow. Preview Interface The workflow preview interface will open, allowing you to interact with your agent. Test with a YouTube URL Paste a test request like: â https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cpKsogGdem4&pp=ygUPYW5kcmV3IGh1YmVybWFu Summarize this video for me.â Run the Test Click the âRunâ button to execute your request. Approve MCP Usage OpenAI Agent Builder will request permission to use the MCP tool. This ensures transparency about external API usage. Grant Permission Click âApproveâ to allow the agent to fetch the YouTube transcript. Success! The agent will fetch the transcript using TranscriptAPI and process it according to your instructions. Advanced Configuration Section titled âAdvanced Configurationâ Available Tools Section titled âAvailable Toolsâ Your agent has access to these TranscriptAPI tools: get_youtube_transcript â Fetch transcript as text or JSON. 1 credit. search_youtube â Paginated search for videos or channels. 1 credit/page. get_channel_latest_videos â Latest ~15 videos via RSS. Free. search_channel_videos â Paginated search within a specific channel. 1 credit/page. list_channel_videos â Paginated channel uploads. 1 credit/page. list_playlist_videos â Paginated playlist videos. 1 credit/page. See Available Tools for full parameter reference and examples. Agent Instructions Example Section titled âAgent Instructions Exampleâ Update your agent instructions to take advantage of the full tool suite: âYou have access to TranscriptAPI tools. You can search YouTube, browse channels, list playlists, and fetch transcripts. When a user asks about a topic, search for relevant videos first, then fetch transcripts for the most promising results.â Setting Response Formats Section titled âSetting Response Formatsâ You can configure how the transcript tool returns data by using its parameters: format : Choose between "text" (markdown) or "json" (structured data) include_timestamp : Set to true or false for timestamp inclusion send_metadata : Include video title, author, and thumbnail information Troubleshooting Section titled âTroubleshootingâ Authentication Issues Section titled âAuthentication Issuesâ Problem : âInvalid API keyâ error Solution : Verify your API key starts with sk_ Check for extra spaces when copying Ensure the key is active in your TranscriptAPI dashboard Credit Errors Section titled âCredit Errorsâ Problem : âPayment required - no credits remainingâ Solution : Purchase credits or upgrade your plan Transcript Not Available Section titled âTranscript Not Availableâ Problem : â404 - Transcript not foundâ Possible Causes : Video has no captions/subtitles Video is private or age-restricted Video was recently uploaded (captions pending) Regional restrictions apply Rate Limiting Section titled âRate Limitingâ Problem : â429 - Too many requestsâ Solution : Wait 60 seconds before retrying Implement delays between batch requests Check your rate limit status in the dashboard Next Steps Section titled âNext Stepsâ Now that youâve successfully integrated TranscriptAPI with OpenAI Agent Builder: Explore Advanced Features : Try different parameter combinations for optimal results Build Complex Workflows : Combine transcript fetching with other AI capabilities Monitor Usage : Track your credit consumption and API performance Join the Community : Share your workflows and learn from others Ready to build more sophisticated agents?
